subject.title: Add atomic claim/lease primitives for concurrent cron job dispatch and removal

question: Which public cron dispatch/removal contract should OpenClaw support for jobs that may be in-flight: a narrow CAS/if-unclaimed remove, a full lease-token claim API, or no new core API for now?
rationale: The implementation is not blocked by a narrow code location; it is blocked by public RPC, CLI, stored-state, and exit-code semantics that need maintainer intent before automation should change core cron behavior.

options.title: Add narrow remove preconditions
options.body: Add `cron rm --if-unclaimed` or an expected-state/version check around existing `runningAtMs` state, with a documented conflict result and focused concurrency tests.

options.title: Design full lease tokens
options.body: Expose claim tokens, expiry, holder metadata, and lease validation through show/remove/run paths, accepting a broader API and persisted-state contract.

options.title: Decline core API for now
options.body: Keep the existing internal scheduler reservations and require external systems to remain idempotent until a stronger core use case is accepted.

recommendation.title: Add narrow remove preconditions
recommendation.body: Add `cron rm --if-unclaimed` or an expected-state/version check around existing `runningAtMs` state, with a documented conflict result and focused concurrency tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron declarative-job and protocol work makes this the clearest available owner for the public API direction question.
